sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y}{x}$ for $x>0$, given $y=6$ when $x=2$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y}=\frac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $\ln|y|=\ln|x|+C$, so $y=Ax$. Using $y=6,x=2$: $A=3$. Solution: $y=3x$.
questions.explanation: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y}=\frac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $\ln|y|=\ln|x|+C$, so $y=Ax$. Using $y=6,x=2$: $A=3$. Solution: $y=3x$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}=3x^2y$, given $y=2$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y}=3x^2\,dx$. Integrate: $\ln|y|=x^3+C$, so $y=Ae^{x^3}$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $A=2$. Solution: $y=2e^{x^3}$.
questions.explanation: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y}=3x^2\,dx$. Integrate: $\ln|y|=x^3+C$, so $y=Ae^{x^3}$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $A=2$. Solution: $y=2e^{x^3}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{2x}{y^2}$, given $y=2$ when $x=0$.
questions.answer: Separate: $y^2\,dy=2x\,dx$. Integrate: $\frac{y^3}{3}=x^2+C$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $C=\frac{8}{3}$. So $y^3=3x^2+8$, giving $y=(3x^2+8)^{1/3}$.
questions.explanation: Separate: $y^2\,dy=2x\,dx$. Integrate: $\frac{y^3}{3}=x^2+C$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $C=\frac{8}{3}$. So $y^3=3x^2+8$, giving $y=(3x^2+8)^{1/3}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{y^2}{x}$ for $x>0$, given $y=1$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y^2}=\frac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $-\frac{1}{y}=\ln|x|+C$. Using $y=1,x=1$: $C=-1$. So $-\frac{1}{y}=\ln x-1$, giving $y=\frac{1}{1-\ln x}$.
questions.explanation: Separate: $\frac{dy}{y^2}=\frac{dx}{x}$. Integrate: $-\frac{1}{y}=\ln|x|+C$. Using $y=1,x=1$: $C=-1$. So $-\frac{1}{y}=\ln x-1$, giving $y=\frac{1}{1-\ln x}$.

questions.q: The rate of decrease of a quantity $Q$ is proportional to $Q$ itself. Write a differential equation for $\frac{dQ}{dt}$, using $k>0$ as the constant of proportionality.
questions.target: Forming differential equations from a description
questions.answer: $\frac{dQ}{dt}=-kQ$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{dQ}{dt}=-kQ$.

questions.q: A tank drains so that the rate of decrease of its volume $V$ is proportional to $\sqrt{V}$. Write a differential equation for $\frac{dV}{dt}$, using $k>0$.
questions.target: Forming differential equations from a description
questions.answer: $\frac{dV}{dt}=-k\sqrt{V}$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{dV}{dt}=-k\sqrt{V}$.

questions.q: A chemical reaction's concentration $C$ decreases at a rate proportional to the square of the concentration. Write a differential equation for $\frac{dC}{dt}$, using $k>0$.
questions.target: Forming differential equations from a description
questions.answer: $\frac{dC}{dt}=-kC^2$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{dC}{dt}=-kC^2$.

sections.heading: Part II — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Multi-Step Application (8–14)

questions.q: A population $P$ satisfies $\frac{dP}{dt}=0.08P$. If $P=500$ when $t=0$, find $P$ when $t=10$, to the nearest whole number.
questions.target: Solving modeling equations with initial conditions

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dV}{dt}=-k\sqrt{V}$ (from the tank problem above), given $V(0)=V_0$.
questions.target: Solving modeling equations with initial conditions
questions.answer: Separate: $V^{-1/2}\,dV=-k\,dt$. Integrate: $2\sqrt{V}=-kt+C$. Using $V(0)=V_0$: $C=2\sqrt{V_0}$. So $\sqrt{V}=\sqrt{V_0}-\frac{kt}{2}$, giving $V(t)=\left(\sqrt{V_0}-\frac{kt}{2}\right)^2$.
questions.explanation: Separate: $V^{-1/2}\,dV=-k\,dt$. Integrate: $2\sqrt{V}=-kt+C$. Using $V(0)=V_0$: $C=2\sqrt{V_0}$. So $\sqrt{V}=\sqrt{V_0}-\frac{kt}{2}$, giving $V(t)=\left(\sqrt{V_0}-\frac{kt}{2}\right)^2$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}+3y=12$ using an integrating factor, given $y=2$ when $x=0$.
questions.target: First-order linear differential equations using an integrating factor
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{3x}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{3x})=12e^{3x}$. Integrate: $ye^{3x}=4e^{3x}+C$, so $y=4+Ce^{-3x}$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $C=-2$. Solution: $y=4-2e^{-3x}$.
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: $e^{3x}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{3x})=12e^{3x}$. Integrate: $ye^{3x}=4e^{3x}+C$, so $y=4+Ce^{-3x}$. Using $y=2,x=0$: $C=-2$. Solution: $y=4-2e^{-3x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}-2y=e^{3x}$ using an integrating factor, given $y=1$ when $x=0$.
questions.target: First-order linear differential equations using an integrating factor
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{-2x}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{-2x})=e^{3x}e^{-2x}=e^x$. Integrate: $ye^{-2x}=e^x+C$, so $y=e^{3x}+Ce^{2x}$. Using $y=1,x=0$: $C=0$. Solution: $y=e^{3x}$.
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: $e^{-2x}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{-2x})=e^{3x}e^{-2x}=e^x$. Integrate: $ye^{-2x}=e^x+C$, so $y=e^{3x}+Ce^{2x}$. Using $y=1,x=0$: $C=0$. Solution: $y=e^{3x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}+y=5$ using an integrating factor, given $y=0$ when $x=0$.
questions.target: First-order linear differential equations using an integrating factor
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^x$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^x)=5e^x$. Integrate: $ye^x=5e^x+C$, so $y=5+Ce^{-x}$. Using $y=0,x=0$: $C=-5$. Solution: $y=5-5e^{-x}$.
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: $e^x$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^x)=5e^x$. Integrate: $ye^x=5e^x+C$, so $y=5+Ce^{-x}$. Using $y=0,x=0$: $C=-5$. Solution: $y=5-5e^{-x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}+4y=8$ using an integrating factor, given $y=3$ when $x=0$.
questions.target: First-order linear differential equations using an integrating factor
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{4x}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{4x})=8e^{4x}$. Integrate: $ye^{4x}=2e^{4x}+C$, so $y=2+Ce^{-4x}$. Using $y=3,x=0$: $C=1$. Solution: $y=2+e^{-4x}$.
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: $e^{4x}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(ye^{4x})=8e^{4x}$. Integrate: $ye^{4x}=2e^{4x}+C$, so $y=2+Ce^{-4x}$. Using $y=3,x=0$: $C=1$. Solution: $y=2+e^{-4x}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x}=x^2$ for $x>0$ using an integrating factor, given $y=1$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{\int\frac{1}{x}dx}=x$. $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=x^3$. Integrate: $xy=\frac{x^4}{4}+C$, so $y=\frac{x^3}{4}+\frac{C}{x}$. Using $y=1,x=1$: $C=\frac{3}{4}$. Solution: $y=\frac{x^3}{4}+\frac{3}{4x}$.
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: $e^{\int\frac{1}{x}dx}=x$. $\frac{d}{dx}(xy)=x^3$. Integrate: $xy=\frac{x^4}{4}+C$, so $y=\frac{x^3}{4}+\frac{C}{x}$. Using $y=1,x=1$: $C=\frac{3}{4}$. Solution: $y=\frac{x^3}{4}+\frac{3}{4x}$.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dx}-\frac{2y}{x}=x^3$ for $x>0$ using an integrating factor, given $y=3$ when $x=1$.
questions.answer: Integrating factor: $e^{\int-\frac{2}{x}dx}=x^{-2}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(yx^{-2})=x$. Integrate: $yx^{-2}=\frac{x^2}{2}+C$, so $y=\frac{x^4}{2}+Cx^2$. Using $y=3,x=1$: $C=\frac{5}{2}$. Solution: $y=\frac{x^4}{2}+\frac{5}{2}x^2$.
questions.explanation: Integrating factor: $e^{\int-\frac{2}{x}dx}=x^{-2}$. $\frac{d}{dx}(yx^{-2})=x$. Integrate: $yx^{-2}=\frac{x^2}{2}+C$, so $y=\frac{x^4}{2}+Cx^2$. Using $y=3,x=1$: $C=\frac{5}{2}$. Solution: $y=\frac{x^4}{2}+\frac{5}{2}x^2$.

questions.q: Verify that $y=3e^{2x}$ satisfies $\frac{dy}{dx}-2y=0$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dx}=6e^{2x}$. Substituting: $6e^{2x}-2(3e^{2x})=6e^{2x}-6e^{2x}=0$, confirming the equation is satisfied.
questions.explanation: $\frac{dy}{dx}=6e^{2x}$. Substituting: $6e^{2x}-2(3e^{2x})=6e^{2x}-6e^{2x}=0$, confirming the equation is satisfied.

questions.q: Verify that $y=x^2+Ce^{-x}$ is a general solution of $\frac{dy}{dx}+y=x^2+2x$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dx}=2x-Ce^{-x}$. Substituting: $(2x-Ce^{-x})+(x^2+Ce^{-x})=2x+x^2$, which matches the right-hand side $x^2+2x$ exactly, confirming the equation is satisfied for any constant $C$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{dy}{dx}=2x-Ce^{-x}$. Substituting: $(2x-Ce^{-x})+(x^2+Ce^{-x})=2x+x^2$, which matches the right-hand side $x^2+2x$ exactly, confirming the equation is satisfied for any constant $C$.

questions.q: Verify that $y=\frac{1}{2}\sin(2x)$ satisfies $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}+4y=0$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos(2x)$. $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-2\sin(2x)$. Substituting: $-2\sin(2x)+4\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin(2x)\right)=-2\sin(2x)+2\sin(2x)=0$, confirming the equation is satisfied.
questions.explanation: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\cos(2x)$. $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-2\sin(2x)$. Substituting: $-2\sin(2x)+4\left(\frac{1}{2}\sin(2x)\right)=-2\sin(2x)+2\sin(2x)=0$, confirming the equation is satisfied.

questions.q: Find the general solution of $\frac{dy}{dx}=4x^3-6x$, and explain what determines a particular solution from this family.
questions.answer: Integrating directly: $y=x^4-3x^2+C$. A particular solution is obtained by specifying one point that the curve must pass through, which fixes the value of the arbitrary constant $C$.
questions.explanation: Integrating directly: $y=x^4-3x^2+C$. A particular solution is obtained by specifying one point that the curve must pass through, which fixes the value of the arbitrary constant $C$.

questions.q: A curve satisfies $\frac{dy}{dx}=6x^2-4$ and passes through $(1,-1)$. Find the equation of this particular solution.
questions.answer: $y=2x^3-4x+C$. Using $(1,-1)$: $-1=2-4+C\Rightarrow C=1$. Solution: $y=2x^3-4x+1$.
questions.explanation: $y=2x^3-4x+C$. Using $(1,-1)$: $-1=2-4+C\Rightarrow C=1$. Solution: $y=2x^3-4x+1$.

sections.heading: Part IV — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Concept Mastery (21–28)

questions.q: Solve the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x}{y}$ with initial condition $y(0) = 4$.
questions.answer: Separate variables: $y dy = 2x dx$. Integrate: $\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2 + C \Rightarrow y^2 = 2x^2 + 2C$. At $(0, 4)$: $16 = 0 + 2C \Rightarrow 2C = 16$. Solution: $y^2 = 2x^2 + 16$.
questions.explanation: Separate variables: $y dy = 2x dx$. Integrate: $\frac{y^2}{2} = x^2 + C \Rightarrow y^2 = 2x^2 + 2C$. At $(0, 4)$: $16 = 0 + 2C \Rightarrow 2C = 16$. Solution: $y^2 = 2x^2 + 16$.

questions.q: Find the general solution of $\frac{dy}{dx} = xy$.
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{y} dy = x dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = \frac{x^2}{2} + c \Rightarrow y = A e^{x^2/2}$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{y} dy = x dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = \frac{x^2}{2} + c \Rightarrow y = A e^{x^2/2}$.

questions.q: Solve the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = 1 + y^2$.
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{1 + y^2} dy = dx \Rightarrow \arctan(y) = x + C \Rightarrow y = \tan(x + C)$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{1 + y^2} dy = dx \Rightarrow \arctan(y) = x + C \Rightarrow y = \tan(x + C)$.

questions.q: Find the general solution of $\frac{dy}{dx} = y(1 - y)$.
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{y(1 - y)} dy = dx \Rightarrow \left(\frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{1 - y}\right) dy = dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| - \ln|1 - y| = x + c \Rightarrow \ln\left|\frac{y}{1 - y}\right| = x + c \Rightarrow \frac{y}{1 - y} = A e^x \Rightarrow y = \frac{A e^x}{1 + A e^x} = \frac{1}{1 + A^{-1}e^{-x}}$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{y(1 - y)} dy = dx \Rightarrow \left(\frac{1}{y} + \frac{1}{1 - y}\right) dy = dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| - \ln|1 - y| = x + c \Rightarrow \ln\left|\frac{y}{1 - y}\right| = x + c \Rightarrow \frac{y}{1 - y} = A e^x \Rightarrow y = \frac{A e^x}{1 + A e^x} = \frac{1}{1 + A^{-1}e^{-x}}$.

questions.q: Solve $\frac{dy}{dt} = k(M - y)$ with $y(0) = 0$ for constant $k, M > 0$.
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{M - y} dy = k dt \Rightarrow -\ln|M - y| = kt + c \Rightarrow M - y = A e^{-kt}$. Since $y(0) = 0$, $A = M$. Thus $y = M(1 - e^{-kt})$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{M - y} dy = k dt \Rightarrow -\ln|M - y| = kt + c \Rightarrow M - y = A e^{-kt}$. Since $y(0) = 0$, $A = M$. Thus $y = M(1 - e^{-kt})$.

questions.q: A chemical reaction produces a substance according to $\frac{dx}{dt} = 2(4 - x)^2$ with $x(0) = 0$. Find $x(t)$.
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{(4 - x)^2} dx = 2 dt \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4 - x} = 2t + C$. At $t = 0$: $1/4 = C$. $\frac{1}{4 - x} = 2t + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{8t + 1}{4} \Rightarrow 4 - x = \frac{4}{8t + 1} \Rightarrow x = 4 - \frac{4}{8t + 1}$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{(4 - x)^2} dx = 2 dt \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4 - x} = 2t + C$. At $t = 0$: $1/4 = C$. $\frac{1}{4 - x} = 2t + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{8t + 1}{4} \Rightarrow 4 - x = \frac{4}{8t + 1} \Rightarrow x = 4 - \frac{4}{8t + 1}$.

questions.q: The rate of decay of a substance is proportional to its remaining mass $m$. Write down the differential equation governing $m(t)$ for constant $k > 0$.
questions.answer: Rate of decay means rate of change is negative and proportional to mass: $\frac{dm}{dt} = -km$.
questions.explanation: Rate of decay means rate of change is negative and proportional to mass: $\frac{dm}{dt} = -km$.

questions.q: Water leaks from a cylindrical tank of cross-sectional area $A$ through a hole at the bottom according to Torricelli's Law: $\frac{dh}{dt} = -c\sqrt{h}$. If initial height is $H$, how long does it take to empty completely?
questions.answer: $h^{-1/2} dh = -c dt \Rightarrow 2\sqrt{h} = -ct + C$. At $t = 0, C = 2\sqrt{H}$. Empty when $h = 0 \Rightarrow 0 = -ct + 2\sqrt{H} \Rightarrow t = \frac{2\sqrt{H}}{c}$.
questions.explanation: $h^{-1/2} dh = -c dt \Rightarrow 2\sqrt{h} = -ct + C$. At $t = 0, C = 2\sqrt{H}$. Empty when $h = 0 \Rightarrow 0 = -ct + 2\sqrt{H} \Rightarrow t = \frac{2\sqrt{H}}{c}$.

sections.heading: Part V — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Application (29–37)

questions.q: A population $P$ grows according to the logistic model $\frac{dP}{dt} = 0.04P\left(1 - \frac{P}{2000}\right)$. What is the carrying capacity of the population?
questions.answer: The logistic equation is $\frac{dP}{dt} = rP(1 - P/K)$, where $K$ is the carrying capacity. Here $K = 2000$.
questions.explanation: The logistic equation is $\frac{dP}{dt} = rP(1 - P/K)$, where $K$ is the carrying capacity. Here $K = 2000$.

questions.q: For the logistic model in the previous question, at what population size $P$ is the growth rate $\frac{dP}{dt}$ maximized?
questions.answer: The growth rate is a quadratic function of $P$ with zeros at 0 and $K$. Its vertex (maximum) occurs at exactly half the carrying capacity: $P = K/2 = 2000/2 = 1000$.
questions.explanation: The growth rate is a quadratic function of $P$ with zeros at 0 and $K$. Its vertex (maximum) occurs at exactly half the carrying capacity: $P = K/2 = 2000/2 = 1000$.

questions.q: Solve the differential equation $x\frac{dy}{dx} = y + 1$ with $y(1) = 3$.
questions.answer: $\frac{1}{y + 1} dy = \frac{1}{x} dx \Rightarrow \ln|y + 1| = \ln|x| + c \Rightarrow y + 1 = A x$. At $(1, 3)$: $3 + 1 = A(1) \Rightarrow A = 4$. Solution is $y = 4x - 1$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{1}{y + 1} dy = \frac{1}{x} dx \Rightarrow \ln|y + 1| = \ln|x| + c \Rightarrow y + 1 = A x$. At $(1, 3)$: $3 + 1 = A(1) \Rightarrow A = 4$. Solution is $y = 4x - 1$.

questions.q: A body cools according to $\frac{dT}{dt} = -0.1(T - 20)$. What does $T(t)$ approach as $t \rightarrow \infty$?
questions.answer: The solution is $T(t) = 20 + C e^{-0.1t}$. As $t \rightarrow \infty$, $e^{-0.1t} \rightarrow 0$, so $T(t) \rightarrow 20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (ambient temperature).
questions.explanation: The solution is $T(t) = 20 + C e^{-0.1t}$. As $t \rightarrow \infty$, $e^{-0.1t} \rightarrow 0$, so $T(t) \rightarrow 20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ (ambient temperature).
